impact: The example does not establish acceptance for an adopted product.
next_action: Define real user workflows, independent expected outcomes and supported platforms; replace example gates.

impact: A local Linux run cannot qualify macOS, hardware, a GUI, or deployment infrastructure.
evidence: Linux/macOS PR jobs are configured; platform and hosting results must be collected after adoption.
next_action: Run the declared platform matrix and real user-entry-point smoke checks, then record a reviewed qualification document.

impact: Local code cannot configure repository rulesets or guarantee reviewers cannot bypass required checks.
evidence: This starter is delivered as an archive, without a hosted GitHub repository.
next_action: Configure the documented required checks and protected baseline/policy review in the adopted repository.

impact: The task-page gate can pass without the pages it is meant to require: CI checks commit order on the PR merge commit, where it reads no commits; order is checked only for tasks marked complete; and a page holding only the 36-byte style marker passes.
evidence: harness/task-artifacts/artifact-harness/blindspots.html cards 01-03 at the archive commit harness/archive.json names (branch showcase/template-history), each reproduced by an independent reviewer in a clean copy.
next_action: None; closed. All three holes are closed in xtask/src/artifacts.rs and xtask/src/history.rs, and pinned in xtask/tests/artifacts.rs. Page order is read from the branch tip that CI passes as handoff --head (and from the second parent when HEAD is a merge on the base): handoff_reads_the_branchs_commits_from_a_pull_request_merge. Before-code order is checked at partial handoff, and a required page needs 1,200 characters outside its tags and styles: a_standard_task_owes_a_brief_before_code. Reopen as a new gap if a brief is found to pass with nothing a reader can use: the gate checks a floor of text, not usefulness.

impact: The scenario and workflow runners can grade only a program that reads its input and exits, and name the example binary in several places. A product that is a long-running service cannot be accepted through them as shipped.
evidence: docs/EVALUATION.md, A held-out build: an agent adopting the template for an HTTP service rewrote xtask/src/workflows.rs and added a service driver (start on port 0, wait for a readiness line, speak HTTP, kill the process group, restart on the same data directory) before it could grade its product. The runner also always sets APP_DATA_DIR, so a scenario cannot test starting without it.
next_action: Add a service transport to the workflow runner along the lines docs/HARNESS.md already describes (start an instance, wait for readiness, exercise flows, capture logs, tear down), and take the binary name from harness/config.json instead of the source.
